<x_0.3271><y_0.007>H E M<x_0.5254><y_0.0266><class_Title>

<x_0.0479><y_0.0289>pelago to Confantinople. It is now called the Darda-
nelles, and is about two miles wide.<x_0.8047><y_0.0578><class_Text>

<x_0.0146><y_0.057>HELM _of a fhip_, is a piece of timber fattened into the
rudder, which comes forward into the fleerage, or
place where the perfon at the helm fleers the flip, by
holding the whiplaff in his hand, which is joined to
the heim. They begin however to be left off, fleering-
wheels being ufed in their room.<x_0.8037><y_0.1422><class_Text>

<x_0.0469><y_0.1414>There are feveral terms in the fea-language relating
to the helm; as, _bear up the helm_; that is, let the
fhip go more large before the wind. _Helm a mid fhip_,
or _right the helm_; that is, keep it even with the
middle of the hip. _Port the helm_, put it over the
the left fide of the fhip. _Starboard the helm_, put it
on the right fide of the fhip.<x_0.8027><y_0.2398><class_Text>

<x_0.0127><y_0.2383>HELMET, an ancient defenlive armour worn by horfemen
both in war and in tournaments. It covered both the
head and face, only leaving an aperture in the front
fecured by bars, which was called the vifor.<x_0.8018><y_0.2953><class_Text>

<x_0.0117><y_0.2945>HELMINTHOLITHUS, in natural hiltory, a name
given by Linnaeus to petrified bodies refembling worms.
Of thefe he reckons four genera. 1. Petrified li-
thophyta, found in the mountains of Sweden. 2. Pe-
trified shells. 3. Petrified zoophytes. 4. Petrified
reptiles.<x_0.8008><y_0.3781><class_Text>

<x_0.0107><y_0.3773>HELMONT, a town of the Netherlands, in the pro-
vince of Dutch Brabant, fituated on the river Aa: E.
long. 5° 40', N. lat. 51° 30'.<x_0.7998><y_0.4203><class_Text>

<x_0.0098><y_0.4195>HELMSTAT, a town of Germany, in the circle of
Lower Saxony, and dukedom of Brunfwie: E. long.
11° 15', N. lat. 52° 20'.<x_0.7988><y_0.4617><class_Text>

<x_0.0088><y_0.4609>HELOTS, in Grecian antiquity, the inhabitants of
Helos, a town of Laconia, conquered by the Spartans;
who made them all prifoners of war, and reduced
them into the condition of flaves.<x_0.8057><y_0.5164><class_Text>

<x_0.0391><y_0.5156>The freemen of Sparta were forbidden the exercife
of any mean or mechanical employment, and therefore
the whole care of fupplying the city with neceflaries
devolved upon the Helots.<x_0.8008><y_0.5719><class_Text>

<x_0.0137><y_0.5711>HELSINGFORD a port-town of Sweden, fituated on
the gulph of Finland, in 24° 6′ E. long. and 60° 8′
N. lat.<x_0.7979><y_0.6125><class_Text>

<x_0.0078><y_0.6133>HELSINGIA, a province of Sweden, bounded by
the Bothnic gulph on the caft, and by Dalecarlia on
the weft.<x_0.7969><y_0.6547><class_Text>

<x_0.0068><y_0.6555>HELSINGIC CHARACTER, a peculiar kind of charac-
ter, found infcribed on ftones in the province of Hel-
fingia : the Runic and Helfingic characters may be easily
transformed into each other.<x_0.7959><y_0.7102><class_Text>

<x_0.0059><y_0.7109>HELSTON, a borough of Cornwall, nine miles fouth-
weft of Falmouth: it fends two members to parlia-
ment.<x_0.7988><y_0.7523><class_Text>

<x_0.0166><y_0.7516>HELVOETSLUYS, a port-town of the united Nether-
lands, fituated in the ifland of Voorn, in the province
of Holland, five miles fouth of the Briel: it is one of
the beft harbours in Holland, and that to which the
Englift packet alway goes.<x_0.8066><y_0.8227><class_Text>

<x_0.0176><y_0.8219>HEMEROBIUS, in zoology, a genus of infects of the
neuroptera order, the characters of which are thefe:
The mouth is furnished with two teeth; the palpi are
four; the wings are deflected, but not plaited ; and
† . 8 L<x_0.8115><y_0.8945><class_Text>
